editorial:
Mirrors (2008) follows Ben Carson, a troubled ex-cop who takes a night security job at a burned-out department store. Soon, the mirrors inside start showing terrifying reflections that don't match reality, and an evil force begins targeting his family. Kiefer Sutherland carries the film with a gritty, desperate performance, and director Alexandre Aja builds a creepy atmosphere with plenty of jump scares and disturbing imagery. The mirror concept is genuinely unsettling, especially in scenes where reflections act on their own and hurt people in the real world.

The movie has some pacing issues and a few plot holes, but the scares are effective and the finale is memorable. If you enjoy supernatural horror with a dark twist, this is a solid pick for a spooky night in. It's best watched in a dark room with the volume turned up. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ben enters the mirror world to rescue his son from the demon, which is the spirit of a possessed woman named Anna Esseker. He manages to get his son out, but the twist is that the real Ben never made it back. The Ben walking around with his family is actually his evil reflection. The real Ben is trapped inside the mirror, pounding on the glass as his family drives away, unaware of the switch.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural horror and jump scares.
